To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“IT security investment decisions should be based on the current and expected future value of information resources and the expected future value of the IT security counterme- sures to protect these information resources.”
the Resource-Based View of IT security investments is a promising approach to understand how the IT protection of organizational resources develops over time.

the protection of organizational information and information technology resources through investments in IT security counterme- sures is a dynamic and complex process that is influenced by a number of factors, including the type of resource to be protected, the type of countermeasure, the organizational context in which the countermeasure is used, and the time period in which the countermeasures are applied.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a theoretical model for IT security investments that is based on a combination of two established theories, and that allows us to synthesize and discuss the literature on IT security investments.

a theoretical and methodological integration of the Resource-Based View of the firm and Organizational Learning Theory in order to provide a theoretical model for IT security investments that is capable of structuring and explaining the economic and technological phenomena of the IT security domain.
the development of a new theoretical model that explains the economic and technological phenomena of IT security investments and that guides future research in the field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IT security investment is a dynamic and complex phenomenon.
the Resource-Based View is a promising theoretical lens to study the economic-technological phenomenon of IT security investments.
the Resource-Based View is a useful theoretical framework for IT security research, but it is not sufficient to explain the economic-technological phenomena in IT security.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the joint application of the Resource-Based View of the Firm and the Organizational learning theory allows to explain the economic-technological phenomena of IT security investments in a comprehensive way.
we suggest a theoretical model of IT security investment that integrates two different theories and that can serve as a basis for further research on IT security.
IT security is a resource and that the development of this resource over time is a process that is influenced by organizational learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IT security investment decisions should consider the organizational learning effects in order to maximize the protection of IT resources.
IT security investments should be considered a dynamic process of organizational learning that is driven by a firm’s resource endowments.
the Resource-Based View can be used to explain how IT security investments affect the value of an organization.
